claim: Onyx v4.7.8 /api/search response does NOT include a `document_id` field — only `citation_id`.
implication: The TASK §1.2 premise ('/api/search 原始结果里同时带 document_id 与 citation_id') is FALSE for this deployment. The mapping key the whole OEI-009 architecture (registry + per-result auth + timebox) depends on does not exist.
stop_trigger: TASK §1.2 step 1.1 verbatim: '若不可映射：立即停手，把结论与候选替代键 (semantic_identifier / 文件名 / 内容 sha256) 写进 REPORT 并等 codex 对齐，不要自行改设计'

per_file_scan.note: engine was unavailable at this run, results empty
alignment_table shows ece_engine_doc_id == raw_citation_id (both '1', '2' for the two uploaded probes)

upload_response_id_fields.public_id: id (user_file.id, UUID) — returned by POST /api/user/projects/file/upload as `document_id`
upload_response_id_fields.note: Neither id appears in the /api/search response at all

candidate_replacement_keys.stability_evidence: OEI-007 alignment_table shows same citation_id per doc across repeated searches; Onyx seems to assign per-source-document stable ids within a session
issues: NOT documented as a stable identifier by Onyx (might be rank-position not stable across queries — needs verification)
Same source doc can return MULTIPLE results (different chunks) → multiple citation_ids for one upload document_id → not a 1:1 mapping
Risk: a doc indexed into N chunks yields N citation_ids, but only ONE upload document_id → can't tell 'this chunk came from doc X'
candidate_replacement_keys.verdict: BROKEN for OEI-009 architecture (1:1 mapping required for per-result auth)

candidate_replacement_keys.stability_evidence: Each Onyx result carries `title` which is the source filename
issues: Two uploads with same filename (e.g. 'report.md' twice) collide
Indexing may produce chunks of same doc under same title — fine, but multiple DOCS sharing filename are indistinguishable
candidate_replacement_keys.verdict: Weak. Sufficient for the 3 demo docs (unique filenames) but not for a general registry. Would require filename uniqueness enforcement at upload time.

candidate_replacement_keys.stability_evidence: Each result carries `content` (full chunk text); sha256 of first N chars could be a stable chunk hash
issues: Hashes the CHUNK, not the source DOC → same source doc → multiple chunk hashes (same problem as citation_id)
Not stable across reindex if chunking params change
No way to map back to upload document_id without storing the mapping server-side
candidate_replacement_keys.verdict: BROKEN. Could be used for chunk-level dedup but not for per-result auth at the document level.

candidate_replacement_keys.key: fetch extra metadata via /file/statuses or /files endpoint (server-side join)
candidate_replacement_keys.stability_evidence: Need empirical verification — does Onyx expose `document_id` in /api/user/projects/files/{project_id}?
issues: Requires an extra round-trip per search result (N+1 problem)
Couples recall to project-level query (not all docs are in a single project)
Performance cost likely unacceptable for the Library's hot path
candidate_replacement_keys.verdict: Workable but adds latency. Needs measurement.

candidate_replacement_keys.key: POST /api/user/projects/file/upload returns document_id; ECE records it in engine_documents at write time (registry written by ECE, NOT derived from search response)
candidate_replacement_keys.stability_evidence: Upload returns `document_id` (user_file.id UUID) which is ECE-controlled
issues: Solves write-path mapping (upload_id ↔ registry row is 1:1)
DOES NOT solve read-path mapping (which user_file.id appeared in /api/search result?) — same as the original problem
Recovers the upload side; still blocked on the recall side
candidate_replacement_keys.verdict: PARTIAL. Required regardless, but doesn't unblock step 1 alone.

verdict: STOP per TASK §1.2 step 1.1. Wait for codex alignment on mapping key before continuing with steps 1.2+ (registry, backfill, per-result auth, timebox, org scope, three design docs).
